```{r setup, message = FALSE}
# ---- Setup ----
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5)
```

This document introduces the dataset, cleans it, builds the features used later, and explores how
EV adoption varies over time and across Washington. The same steps are implemented in Python in
`python/01_data_preparation_eda.ipynb`.

# 1. The dataset

The **Electric Vehicle Population Data** (Washington State Department of Licensing, data.wa.gov, Open
Database License) lists every battery-electric (BEV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) vehicle registered with
the state. This snapshot was last updated on 14 October 2026. The file is stored compressed without the
partial VIN, DOL vehicle ID and point coordinates.

```{r load}
# ZIP code, census tract and legislative district are labels, so they are read as text
raw <- read.csv(gzfile("../data/ev_population.csv.gz"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                check.names = FALSE, na.strings = "",
                colClasses = c("Postal Code" = "character", "2020 GEOID" = "character",
                               "Legislative District" = "character"))
dim(raw)
raw %>% count(`Electric Vehicle Type`, name = "vehicles") %>%
  mutate(percent = round(vehicles / sum(vehicles) * 100, 1))
```

# 2. Data quality

```{r quality}
miss <- colSums(is.na(raw))
miss[miss > 0]
cat("Vehicles registered outside Washington:", sum(raw$State != "WA"), "\n")
cat("Share with electric range recorded as 0:", round(mean(raw$`Electric Range` == 0, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
raw %>% filter(`Model Year` >= 2015) %>% group_by(`Model Year`) %>%
  summarise(share_range_0 = round(mean(`Electric Range` == 0, na.rm = TRUE), 2)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = `Model Year`, values_from = share_range_0)
```

**Interpretation.** Only a few records lack location fields (mostly vehicles registered outside
Washington). Electric range is recorded as 0 ("not yet researched") for
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(raw$"Electric Range" == 0, na.rm = TRUE))` of vehicles, nearly all from model
year 2021 onward, so range cannot be used as a feature for recent vehicles.

# 3. Cleaning and feature engineering

```{r clean}
df <- raw
steps <- data.frame(step = "Raw data", rows = nrow(df))
# (1) Washington registrations only
df <- df %>% filter(State == "WA")
steps <- rbind(steps, data.frame(step = "Keep Washington registrations", rows = nrow(df)))
# (2) Drop rows missing location fields
df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(County), !is.na(`Postal Code`), !is.na(`Electric Utility`),
                    !is.na(`Legislative District`))
steps <- rbind(steps, data.frame(step = "Drop rows missing location fields", rows = nrow(df)))
# (3) Model year 2011 onward
df <- df %>% filter(`Model Year` >= 2011)
steps <- rbind(steps, data.frame(step = "Keep model year 2011 onward", rows = nrow(df)))
steps
```

```{r features}
eastern <- c("Adams", "Asotin", "Benton", "Chelan", "Columbia", "Douglas", "Ferry", "Franklin",
             "Garfield", "Grant", "Kittitas", "Klickitat", "Lincoln", "Okanogan", "Pend Oreille",
             "Spokane", "Stevens", "Walla Walla", "Whitman", "Yakima")
df <- df %>%
  mutate(bev = as.integer(startsWith(`Electric Vehicle Type`, "Battery")),     # (a) outcome
         region = case_when(County %in% c("King", "Snohomish", "Pierce") ~ "Seattle metro",
                            County %in% eastern ~ "Eastern WA",
                            TRUE ~ "Other western WA"),                           # (b) region
         utility = sub("\\|.*$", "", `Electric Utility`),                        # (d) first utility
         tesla = as.integer(Make == "TESLA")) %>%                                # (f) Tesla flag
  group_by(City) %>% mutate(city_evs = n()) %>% ungroup()                        # (c) urbanity proxy

top_util <- names(sort(table(df$utility), decreasing = TRUE))[1:6]
df$utility <- ifelse(df$utility %in% top_util, df$utility, "Other")
top_cty <- names(sort(table(df$County), decreasing = TRUE))[1:15]
df$county_grp <- ifelse(df$County %in% top_cty, df$County, "Other")             # (e) county
df <- df %>% rename(zip = `Postal Code`, model_year = `Model Year`, leg_district = `Legislative District`)

cat(sprintf("Rows: %d; BEV share after cleaning: %.2f%%\n", nrow(df), 100 * mean(df$bev)))
sort(table(df$utility), decreasing = TRUE)
```

# 4. Exploratory analysis

## 4.1 Growth over time and the BEV/PHEV mix

```{r eda-year}
by_year <- df %>% group_by(model_year) %>% summarise(vehicles = n(), bev_share = round(mean(bev), 3))

df %>% count(model_year, type = ifelse(bev == 1, "BEV", "PHEV")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(model_year), n, fill = type)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(BEV = "seagreen", PHEV = "darkorange")) +
  labs(title = "Registered EVs by Model Year", x = "Model year", y = "Vehicles currently registered",
       fill = "Type") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5))

ggplot(by_year, aes(model_year, bev_share)) +
  geom_line(colour = "seagreen") + geom_point(colour = "seagreen") +
  labs(title = "Battery-Electric Share by Model Year", x = "Model year",
       y = "Share of vehicles that are BEV")
by_year
```

**Interpretation.** Registrations peak at `r format(max(by_year$vehicles), big.mark = ",")` vehicles for
model year `r by_year$model_year[which.max(by_year$vehicles)]`. The BEV share is erratic for older model
years and sits around 78–88% from 2019, with a dip for 2024–2025.

## 4.2 Top makes and regions

```{r eda-makes}
top_makes <- df %>% count(Make, sort = TRUE) %>% head(10)
ggplot(top_makes, aes(reorder(Make, n), n)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 10 EV Makes in Washington", x = "Make", y = "Registered vehicles")

reg <- df %>% group_by(region) %>% summarise(vehicles = n(), bev_share = round(mean(bev), 3))
ggplot(reg, aes(reorder(region, bev_share), bev_share)) + geom_col(fill = "seagreen") + coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "BEV Share by Region", x = "Region", y = "Share of vehicles that are BEV")
reg
df %>% group_by(County) %>% summarise(vehicles = n(), bev_share = round(mean(bev), 3)) %>%
  arrange(desc(vehicles)) %>% head(15)
```

**Interpretation.** Tesla holds `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(df$tesla))` of EVs. The Seattle metro has
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(df$region == "Seattle metro"))` of all EVs and the highest BEV share
(`r reg$bev_share[reg$region == "Seattle metro"]`), against
`r reg$bev_share[reg$region == "Eastern WA"]` in eastern Washington.

```{r save}
dir.create("../data/processed", showWarnings = FALSE)
cols <- c("County", "City", "zip", "model_year", "Make", "Model", "Electric Vehicle Type",
          "Electric Range", "leg_district", "bev", "region", "city_evs", "utility", "county_grp", "tesla")
write.csv(df[, cols], "../data/processed/ev_clean_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Saved", nrow(df), "rows\n")
```

# 5. Summary

The cleaned data hold every EV of model year 2011 onward registered in Washington, the same
`r format(nrow(df), big.mark = ",")` vehicles as the Python version. Question 1 classifies BEV vs PHEV
from location and time; Question 2 clusters ZIP-code fleet profiles.
